correctness.rationale: The exact binary split identities are \(a=(a_0+a_1+d)/2\le1\), \(0\le a_0,a_1\le1\). The induction error reduces to \((q^d-1)(1+C a_1)\le Cd\). For \(0\le d\le1\), convexity and \((q-1)(1+C)=C\) suffice. For \(1\le d\le2\), the inequality becomes \(q^{d-1}(1-(q-1)(d-1))\le1\), which follows from \(\log q\le q-1\) and \(\log(1-u)\le-u\). Dyadic conditional means preserve BLO and local essential minima decrease to the original one; Fatou passes the result to \(L^1\). Geometric staircases yield exact mean one and moment \(1/(2-q)\); dyadic block placement realizes each local excess. Geometric divergence covers \(q\ge2\). Finite computation supplements but never replaces the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact objects and implications were compared. Zhang (2026) establishes ordinary all-subinterval BLO tails; Osękowski (2013) establishes ordinary BLO mean-centered absolute oscillations. Osękowski (2014) controls the dyadic maximal operator centered at the root mean and already contains the same sharp scalar constant and staircase, but does not state the exact mean-sensitive affine bound for the lower-centered observable \(\exp(\lambda(f-\operatorname{ess\,inf} f))\). The assessed contribution is the full two-parameter Bellman envelope, not the numerical threshold alone. The full 1996 article was inaccessible and creates residual duplication risk.

value.rationale: The local excess \(a=(\langle f\rangle-\operatorname{ess\,inf}f)/B(f)\) is an intrinsic state parameter in dyadic stopping-time arguments. The theorem determines the complete sharp two-parameter exponential Bellman envelope, including its infinite-moment boundary; this gives precise dyadic \(A_1\) and exponential-integrability calibration at every local excess, rather than only the previously known scalar maximal bound. Exact attainment for every real \(a\in[0,1]\) is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary finite computation.
